newsitem.title: FRANCE: No blank cheques for layoffs - French jobs minister.
newsitem.headline: No blank cheques for layoffs - French jobs minister.

text.p: French Employment Minister Martine Aubry said on Friday the government had no intention of paying out early retirement subsidies to big firms which restructured without equipping staff to seek other types of employment.

"It is unacceptable for big companies in healthy financial situations to make taxpayers pay for restructuring without their making the slightest effort to reconvert regions where there has been a single industrial activity for years and without helping staff to switch activity," she told a news conference.
"If companies content themselves with handing out departure cheques and asking the state to make early retirement payments, that's not a proper social plan and I will not give my consent," she said.
She was responding to a question on her stance in the wake of plans including one by PSA Peugeot Citroen to cut 2,816 posts.
This position applied "to all companies", she said.

Aubry, who heads a beefed-up employment ministry and is "Number Two" to Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin, said she would review legislation of company layoffs from the point of view of the legal framework and employee protection.
"The rules are not always respected," she said at her first news conference since taking up the post.
